This code will introduce an user to ARIMA model used in infectious disease modeling. 



```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

# code for forecasting diarrhoea cases among under five children in Malawi using ARIMA model

```{r cars}

install.packages("rio")
install.packages("tidyverse")
install.packages("forecast")
install.packages("here")
install.packages("tseries")
install.packages("ggplots")
install.packages("zoo")

# calling fackages to be used in the sesion using the library() function 

library(forecast) # for forecating the cases
library(tidyverse) # data management 
library(rio) # This package help with  importing data set in more format
library(here) # This package help with file path and directory 
library(tseries) # for changing data frame object to time series object
library(ggplot2)
library(zoo)




```

# loading data

```{r pressure, echo=FALSE}

# loading data from 

diarrhoea_df<- import(here("data/Diarrhoea_u5_2023_2025_data.csv")) |> 
  mutate(year=as.Date(year, format="%Y-%B-%M")) # change the column of year to date format 

# change the list to data.frame object

diarrhoea_df <- as.data.frame(diarrhoea_df)


```



# calculating ARIMA model for forecasting diarrhoea cases among under five children in Malawi considering seasonality 


```{r}

## ==========================================================================
## Malawi Diarrhoea Cases:  season ARIMA Forecast for 2026
## ==========================================================================
## Workflow:
##  1. Prepare time series
##  2. Handle missing values
##  3. Inspect for structural breaks (e.g. COVID-era reporting disruption)
##  4. Check stationarity (non-seasonal AND seasonal)
##  5. Validate model on a held-out test set (train/test split)
##  6. Fit final SARIMA model on full data
##  7. Diagnostic checks on residuals
##  8. Forecast 12 months ahead
##  9. Plot and export results
## ==========================================================================



# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Step 1: Convert to time series
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Adjust start = c(year, month) to match your actual first observation
diarrhoea_ts <- ts(diarrhoea_df$cases, start = c(2020, 1), frequency = 12)

autoplot(diarrhoea_ts) +
  ggtitle("Malawi Diarrhoea Cases: Full Observed Series") +
  xlab("Time") + ylab("Number of Cases") +
  theme_minimal()

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Step 2: Handle missing values
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
if (anyNA(diarrhoea_ts)) {
  message("Missing values detected — interpolating.")
  diarrhoea_ts <- na.interp(diarrhoea_ts)
}

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Step 3: Check for structural breaks / outliers (e.g. COVID-era disruption)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# tsoutliers() flags points that deviate sharply from the modelled series.
# Inspect these manually before deciding whether to adjust or trim.
outlier_check <- tsoutliers(diarrhoea_ts)
print(outlier_check)

# If a COVID-era disruption period is confirmed (e.g. 2020-04 to 2020-12
# had reporting gaps or reporting-system distortion rather than true
# incidence change), consider ONE of the following before proceeding:
#
# Option A — trim the disrupted period out entirely: this not to consider the period as example below
# diarrhoea_ts <- window(diarrhoea_ts, start = c(2021, 1))
#
# Option B — replace flagged outlier points with interpolated values:
# diarrhoea_ts[outlier_check$index] <- outlier_check$replacements
#
# Decide based on visual inspection of the plot above and your knowledge
# of what happened to reporting in that period. Document whichever choice
# you make, since it materially affects the seasonal pattern learned below.

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Step 4: Check stationarity — non-seasonal AND seasonal
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# ADF test: checks for a non-seasonal unit root only.
adf_test <- adf.test(diarrhoea_ts)
print(adf_test)
# p > 0.05 => fail to reject null of non-stationarity (non-seasonal sense)

# Differencing needed (auto.arima will do this internally, but useful to see)
cat("Suggested non-seasonal differences (ndiffs):", ndiffs(diarrhoea_ts), "\n")
cat("Suggested seasonal differences (nsdiffs):   ", nsdiffs(diarrhoea_ts), "\n")

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Step 5: Out-of-sample validation (train/test split)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Hold out the most recent 6 months as a test set to check forecast accuracy
# before trusting the final 12-month-ahead projection.
n_test <- 6
train_end <- time(diarrhoea_ts)[length(diarrhoea_ts) - n_test]

train <- window(diarrhoea_ts, end = train_end)
test  <- window(diarrhoea_ts, start = time(diarrhoea_ts)[length(diarrhoea_ts) - n_test + 1])

fit_train <- auto.arima(
  train,
  stepwise = FALSE,
  approximation = FALSE,
  seasonal = TRUE
)

fc_test <- forecast(fit_train, h = n_test)

cat("\n--- Out-of-sample accuracy (last", n_test, "months held out) ---\n")
print(accuracy(fc_test, test))

autoplot(fc_test) +
  autolayer(test, series = "Actual") +
  ggtitle("Validation: Forecast vs Actual (Held-Out Period)") +
  xlab("Time") + ylab("Number of Cases") +
  theme_minimal()

# Review the RMSE / MAPE above. If MAPE is very high (e.g. >30-40%),
# treat the final forecast with caution and say so in your report —
# especially given the series likely has fewer than 8 full seasonal
# cycles, which limits how reliably SARIMA can estimate seasonality.

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Step 6: Fit final model on the FULL series
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
fit <- auto.arima(
  diarrhoea_ts,
  stepwise = FALSE,
  approximation = FALSE,
  seasonal = TRUE,
  trace = TRUE
)

summary(fit)

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Step 7: Diagnostic checks
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
checkresiduals(fit)
# Check the printed Ljung-Box p-value: want p > 0.05, indicating residuals
# are consistent with white noise (no leftover structure the model missed).

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Step 8: Forecast next 12 periods
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
future_forecast <- forecast(fit, h = 12)# h is the length in time.
summary(future_forecast)

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Step 9: Plot final forecast
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Confirm this title matches your actual forecast window: 12 months
# beyond your LAST observed data point, not necessarily calendar year 2026.
# last_obs_time <- time(diarrhoea_ts)[length(diarrhoea_ts)]
# last_obs_label <- paste0(floor(last_obs_time), "-", cycle(diarrhoea_ts)[length(diarrhoea_ts)])

autoplot(future_forecast) +
  ggtitle(paste0("Malawi 12-Month Forecast of Diarrhoea Cases\n",
                  "(from ", last_obs_label, " onward)")) +
  xlab("Time") + ylab("Number of Cases") +
  theme_minimal()

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Optional: export forecast table for the report
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
forecast_df <- data.frame(
  date       = as.Date(time(future_forecast$mean)),
  forecast   = as.numeric(future_forecast$mean),
  lower_80   = as.numeric(future_forecast$lower[, 1]),
  upper_80   = as.numeric(future_forecast$upper[, 1]),
  lower_95   = as.numeric(future_forecast$lower[, 2]),
  upper_95   = as.numeric(future_forecast$upper[, 2])
)

# saving the predicted values
write.csv(forecast_df, "diarrhoea_forecast_2026.csv", row.names = FALSE)

```
